title: TF module drift detection and compatibility playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a practical playbook for detecting, mitigating, and rolling out Terraform module interface changes (variables/outputs) across private deployments (VPC+IAM+K8s primitives). Focus: avoid silent breaking changes, reduce upgrade friction for on-prem and VPC customers, and provide an automated signal path for early detection of drift at both repo and cluster level.

Key goals (quick):
- Catch incompatible variable/output changes before consumers update
- Provide targeted canary upgrade steps and automated CI gates
- Standardize deprecation policies and fallback variable mechanism
- Detect runtime drift (state drift vs. module contract drift) and alert owners

High-level approach:
1) Prevent: strong module contract rules + automated change-linting in PRs.
2) Detect: CI and repo-level static checks, runtime drift detectors comparing desired vs actual resources, and output-compat tests.
3) Mitigate: automated compatibility shims, gradual rollout & canary, clear rollback path + quick fixes (patch modules).

Module contract rules (must-ships in every module):
- variables.tf must include 'compatibility' meta-comments for each variable if changing semantics (e.g., allowed-values change).
- outputs must be marked stable/experimental/deprecated using a simple comment token: #redwood:stable | #redwood:deprecated:2025-01-01
- keep old outputs for at least one semver minor cycle and provide mapping shims where possible.
- No removal of outputs without a deprecation cycle documented in PR description and a JIRA/Ticket created.

Semantic change taxonomy (signal levels):
- Level 0 (safe): internal refactor, no name/shape change to variables/outputs.
- Level 1 (non-breaking extension): add optional var or new output (backwards compatible).
- Level 2 (soft breaking): change default value, restrict allowed values — requires consumer opt-in test.
- Level 3 (hard breaking): rename/remove variable/output, change type — requires deprecation cycle + migrations.

CI checks and gating (PR-time):
- Schema diff: run a terraform-schema-diff tool that compares variables/outputs vs latest published module release. Fail PRs that introduce Level 3 changes unless matched with a deprecation ticket.
- Output usage map: lightweight grep across dependent modules/apps to show callsites for outputs being removed/renamed.
- Automated compatibility tests: run a small harness that applies module with existing example variables and verifies expected outputs. Use ephemeral AWS/GCP/Tanzu workspaces where feasible.
- Semantic version bump enforcement: PR must include target semver bump (patch/minor/major) and rationale.

Runtime drift detection (cluster-level):
- Two signals to compute daily:
  - Desired-vs-Observed: plan/apply drift check run against customer-managed state (where permitted) or internal test clusters that mirror customer config.
  - Output-contract monitor: after upgrades, run a smoke job that exercises dependent stacks and verifies outputs are present and typed as expected.
- Alerting: Slack channel + PagerDuty policy for Level 3 changes detected in production clusters.

Compatibility shims and fallback patterns (practical recipes):
- Variable aliasing pattern: introduce new variable (foo_bar_v2) but accept old name (foo_bar) via locals mapping so both work for one cycle.
- Output shim: keep old output name but route to computed value and mark deprecated in output description. Example: output "load_balancer_ip" { value = module.nlb.ip #redwood:deprecated:2025-02-01 }
- Type-flexible outputs: when changing output type (string -> list), expose a stable shape wrapper output e.g. output "x_as_list" always returns list([…]) and mark prior scalar output deprecated.

Upgrade & rollout plan (canary pattern for module releases):
- Phase 0: Pre-flight
  - Run schema-diff across internal consumers and produce a 'risk report'.
  - Execute compatibility tests in a CI ephemeral environment.
  - Notify downstream owners (automated emails from PR tag).
- Phase 1: Canary non-critical namespace (1-2 test clusters or 5% of internal customers).
  - Apply module release with module registry pinning and run post-deploy smoke tests.
  - Monitor output-contract monitor for 48 hours.
- Phase 2: Broad internal rollout (remaining internal clusters).
- Phase 3: Customer opt-in or automated upgrade window depending on contract.
- Rollback: immediate terraform apply using pinned previous module version in case of critical failures. Maintain a script that reverts module source refs across dependent repos.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Unit: schema-diff unit tests for variable/output changes.
- Integration: apply module with example below (VPC+subnets+ngw) and verify outputs.
- Regression: run consumer stacks against published module versions and expect no output missing errors.

Example consumer-safe variable change (pattern):
- Goal: rename var "private_subnet_ids" -> "subnet_ids_private"
- Steps:
  1) Add new var 'subnet_ids_private' optional = true, description referencing migration.
  2) In module use locals { subnet_ids = coalesce(var.subnet_ids_private, var.private_subnet_ids) }
  3) Keep old var present but mark comment #redwood:deprecated:2025-01-15 and update README migration section.
  4) Bump module minor version and run CI compatibility tests.

Example of minimal schema lint report (text):
- changed_outputs:
  - removed: none
  - renamed: none
  - added: ["nlb_listener_arn_v2"]
- changed_variables:
  - changed_defaults: ["enable_flow_logs"]
  - renamed_candidates: ["private_subnet_ids -> subnet_ids_private"]
- recommended_semver: minor

Operational playbook for detected drift: (short list)
- If Level 0 or 1: auto-create PR to library with mapping shim, schedule minor release.
- If Level 2: open RFC ticket, run consumer-impact job, assign follow-up.
- If Level 3 in production: trigger incident playbook: annotate affected clusters, roll back to pinned module, notify CS & security if customer-facing.

Data retention and audit traces:
- Keep schema-diff artifacts per PR for 180 days.
- All automated detection alerts must include module git ref, registry version, commit SHA, and list of impacted consumers.

Open questions / TODOs (needs work before finalizing):
- How to handle consumer repos that pin module to a branch instead of versioned registry? (proposal: require registry pinning for modules under supported layer)
- Cost/latency tradeoffs for running ephemeral integration applies per PR vs nightly batch for large modules.
- Determine precise deprecation windows per module class (networking vs infra vs secrets) — propose 90 days for infra, 180 days for networking-sensitive outputs.

Appendix: quick checklist for module maintainers (copyable):
- [ ] Add compatibility section to PR description if touching variables/outputs
- [ ] Run schema-diff and attach results to PR
- [ ] Add semver bump and update CHANGELOG with migration steps
- [ ] Create deprecation ticket for any removal/rename (link in PR)
- [ ] Ensure at least one consumer-run integration test passes

End of doc.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive — aim to reduce on-prem upgrade incidents and provide automated signals for drift. Feedback: add any missing CI hooks we should add to the infra-modules repo and propose exact Slack/pager routing for production Level 3 alerts.
